**My thinking:**

I have always farmed this land the same way my mother did, and her mother before her. We are in Quzhou — flat land, good enough soil, but water is the constant worry. Everyone here grows winter wheat and summer maize on the same plot, one after the other. That is what I know, that is what the grain buyer at the township will take, and that is what keeps my family fed. I do not experiment with new crops I do not know.

I have about 6 mu of farmland. I will plant all of it to wheat in the autumn and then maize right after the wheat harvest in June. I have done this my whole life.

For seed, I buy whatever the village seed shop has — the improved wheat variety they always recommend, and a hybrid maize seed. I do not save my own seed anymore; the shop seed yields better.

For fertilizer, I buy a bag of compound fertilizer (nitrogen-phosphorus-potassium together) before planting, and then I put urea on top when the wheat is jointing. The maize I side-dress with urea when it's knee-high. That is what the neighbors do and the crops come out fine.

Water is expensive and the well is shared. But I will not risk losing the wheat — I water before winter, at jointing, at heading, and once more if it looks dry. Maize gets summer rain mostly; I water once if needed.

I hire a machine for rotary tillage before each planting. I spray herbicide on the wheat in winter and aphids in spring. Maize just needs one spray for corn borer.
